payload.reason: The evidence provides specific details about the inference models used to estimate socioeconomic status (SES) based on various data sources and methodologies.

claims.text: The inference model for estimating SES relies on three datasets: socioeconomic census data, crawled profession information, and expert annotated Google Street View images of users' home locations.
The model uses user semantics and profile information from Twitter to predict SES, demonstrating a trade-off between prediction quality and scalability.
The inference task is framed as a two-way classification problem, categorizing users into lower and higher SES classes based on income distributions.
